steps.title: Answers
steps.body:
**Yes.** CVS Health’s 2022 Form 10-K describes several significant legal matters that were still ongoing or unresolved at year-end:

- **Opioid litigation:** CVS reported nationwide federal and state cases. A 2021 jury found chain pharmacies liable, and in 2022 the court entered a **$651 million judgment jointly against three defendants**; CVS was appealing and had not accrued a liability for that judgment. CVS also recorded **$5.2 billion and $99 million in opioid-related charges in 2022** for settlements and other claims. A proposed settlement with states and subdivisions could require up to **$4.3 billion plus $625 million in fees and costs**, and a tribal settlement up to **$131 million**. The filing says private litigation would continue and ultimate losses remained uncertain.  
- **Government investigations:** A DOJ subpoena in **2020** and a further CID in **2022** sought information about CVS’s opioid and controlled-substance practices; CVS said it was responding. The filing also describes ongoing lawsuits and investigations into PBM pricing and manufacturer rebates.
- **Other continuing cases:** The filing describes securities and ERISA cases concerning CVS’s long-term-care business. Some had been dismissed, but appeals, stays, or other claims remained; the ERISA case was dismissed with prejudice in October 2022 and appealed.

The filing cautions that outcomes could materially affect CVS’s business, results, or cash flows, although it says it could not estimate the total possible loss for all opioid litigation. **Pages 173–177.**

steps.title: Answers
steps.body:
**Yes.** CVS Health disclosed significant ongoing litigation and investigations associated with 2020, 2021 and 2022, though it did not say that every matter was individually material.

- **2020:** The company received a DOJ administrative subpoena concerning prescription opioids and controlled substances; it also disclosed two ERISA class actions filed in 2020 that remained active after amended complaints were filed and CVS moved to dismiss (pp. 175, 177).
- **2021–2022:** CVS was found liable with other chain pharmacies in an opioid trial in 2021. A 2022 judgment imposed $651 million jointly on the defendants, payable over 15 years; CVS said it was appealing and had not accrued a liability (p. 174).
- **Ongoing matters:** CVS also described multiple PBM drug-pricing and rebate lawsuits and related investigations, as well as opioid cases in federal and state courts (pp. 173–174). The filing warns that outcomes of certain lawsuits or governmental proceedings could materially affect the company (p. 173).

steps.body:
**Yes.** CVS Health disclosed several significant ongoing legal matters. The most financially consequential were opioid-related claims: the company recorded **$5.803 billion in opioid litigation charges in 2022**. A 2021 jury judgment of **$651 million** was under appeal, and the 2022 government and tribal settlement processes did not end private-plaintiff litigation. The filing also describes ongoing PBM pricing and rebate lawsuits and investigations, pharmacy-pricing lawsuits, and Medicare risk-adjustment investigations. Separately, ERISA class actions filed in 2020 over the LTC business remained in litigation, with an appeal pending in 2022.

The company cautioned that legal outcomes were uncertain; it stated that accrued amounts for outstanding legal matters were not material to its financial condition, while noting that unanticipated outcomes could materially affect results. (pp. 75, 171–175)

steps.title: Answers
steps.body:
**Yes.** CVS reported significant ongoing litigation spanning 2020–2022, with opioid-related cases the most financially consequential:

- **2021–2022 opioid case:** After a 2021 jury verdict, a federal court entered a **$651 million judgment in 2022** against three pharmacy defendants. CVS said it was appealing and had not accrued a liability for that judgment. Private opioid litigation also continued despite 2022 agreements intended to resolve substantially all claims by participating governmental entities and tribes. (p. 174)
- **Material financial exposure:** CVS recorded **$5.803 billion in opioid litigation charges in 2022**. It said the ultimate outcome of the opioid matters could materially affect its business, financial condition, results or cash flows. (pp. 79–80, 175)
- **Matters dating to 2020:** The DOJ served CVS with a subpoena in 2020 concerning opioid and controlled-substance practices, followed by a similar CID in 2022; CVS said it was responding. Separately, ERISA class actions filed in 2020 were dismissed in 2022, but plaintiffs appealed. (pp. 175, 177)

**Qualification:** CVS said its accruals for other outstanding legal matters were not material to its financial condition and that it did not believe pending matters, after reserves and indemnification, would materially harm its financial position. (p. 173)
